title: Scheherazade
hook: A storyteller saves her life one tale at a time. Her voice is a solo violin.

painting.title: The Ninth Wave
painting.pairingNote: Survivors cling to the mast of a wrecked ship as the sea calms at sunrise, the shipwreck and stillness of Scheherazade’s last pages, painted by Russia’s great painter of the sea.

facts: Rimsky-Korsakov wrote *Scheherazade* in the summer of 1888, at a country house south of St Petersburg. His score is dated between 4 June and 7 August.

It is based on the frame story of *The Thousand and One Nights*, which he printed in the score. The Sultan Shahriar, convinced that all women are faithless, has each new wife killed after the wedding night. Scheherazade saves her life by telling him a story every night, for a thousand and one nights, until he gives up his vow.

The two characters have their own themes. The Sultan is a heavy phrase played in [[unison|unison]] by low brass and strings. Scheherazade is a solo violin, winding and ornate, over a harp. She returns between the tales, like a storyteller taking a breath.
He gave the movements titles, then withdrew them. He wanted listeners to hear one Eastern fairy tale full of wonders, not four separate pictures. The titles are still used.
As a young naval officer, Rimsky-Korsakov had spent almost three years at sea. The sea fills the first and last movements.
bigPicture.inOneLine: the sea (I), a wanderer’s tale (II), a love song (III), a festival and a shipwreck (IV).

movements.heading: The Sea and Sinbad's Ship
movements.title: The Sea and Sinbad's Ship
movements.tempo: Largo e maestoso – Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: The Sultan’s stern theme, then Scheherazade’s violin, then the sea. The Sultan’s theme itself becomes the swell of the waves. The whole movement rolls like a ship under sail.

mainIdeas.name: The Sultan
mainIdeas.description: a loud, heavy phrase that falls step by step, in the low brass and strings.

mainIdeas.name: Scheherazade
mainIdeas.description: a long, curling violin solo over harp chords. Each character is tied to a theme, a [[leitmotif|leitmotif]].

mainIdeas.name: The sea
mainIdeas.description: cellos rocking in broad waves under the Sultan’s theme, now flowing.

stops.hear: Trombones, tuba and low strings together, loud and grim
A few soft chords in the woodwinds
A solo violin, high and free, curling around over harp chords
The cellos start to rock in long waves; the violins sing the Sultan’s theme, now broad and flowing
stops.happening: The sea. Sinbad’s ship sails out

stops.hear: A gentle woodwind melody over calmer water
The solo violin returns for a moment
stops.happening: The storyteller’s voice, before the sea takes over again

stops.hear: The full orchestra swells; brass and cymbals crown the waves

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The waves settle; a flute and the solo violin, very soft
stops.happening: Calm water. The movement ends quietly in E major

movements.heading: The Story of the Kalendar Prince
movements.title: The Story of the Kalendar Prince
movements.summary: A kalendar was a wandering dervish. A playful bassoon tells his story, other instruments retell it, and then the brass interrupt with a call to arms. The most varied movement of the four.

stops.hear: The solo violin and harp
A solo bassoon plays a long, wandering tune with little twists, over soft plucked basses
stops.happening: The kalendar’s tale. The basses play [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]

stops.hear: An oboe takes the same tune, then the violins
stops.happening: The story passes from voice to voice

stops.hear: A sudden trombone fanfare, answered by a [[muted|muted]] trumpet
stops.happening: The Allegro molto: a call to battle

stops.hear: A clarinet, then a bassoon, play free, showy solos while the orchestra waits
A brisk march builds in the full orchestra

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The bassoon’s tune returns, now loud in the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The tale ends in a rush

movements.heading: The Young Prince and the Young Princess
movements.title: The Young Prince and the Young Princess
movements.summary: A love song. A warm melody for the violins alternates with a lighter, dancing tune decorated with drum, tambourine and triangle. Scheherazade’s violin appears in the middle, as if she is reminding the Sultan who is telling the story.

stops.hear: The violins sing a tender, swaying melody; a clarinet decorates it with quick runs
A light, dancing tune in the clarinet and flute; snare drum, tambourine and triangle tap out the rhythm
The first melody returns, fuller
The solo violin and harp, alone
stops.happening: Scheherazade’s voice, in the middle of her own tale

stops.hear: The love melody once more, richer, in the whole orchestra

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Soft echoes of the dance; a quiet close

movements.heading: Festival at Baghdad – The Sea – The Ship Breaks against a Cliff
movements.title: Festival at Baghdad – The Sea – The Ship Breaks against a Cliff Surmounted by a Bronze Horseman
movements.tempo: Allegro molto – Vivo – Allegro non troppo e maestoso
movements.summary: The Sultan and Scheherazade confront each other, then the city erupts in a festival. Themes from earlier movements whirl past. The sea returns, the ship is wrecked on a rock, and in the quiet that follows, the violin has the last word.

stops.hear: The Sultan’s theme, fast and fierce, in the low strings; the solo violin answers with harsh chords
stops.happening: A confrontation. The Sultan is impatient, Scheherazade holds firm

stops.hear: A rapid dance: flutes, strings, tambourine
Earlier tunes fly past in the crowd: the bassoon’s tale from II, the princess’s dance from III
The brass blaze out the sea music from the first movement; huge waves in the strings
A crash of the gong; the trombones hammer out the Sultan’s theme
stops.happening: The ship breaks against the rock

stops.hear: The storm drains away; the waves grow calm

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: The solo violin plays Scheherazade’s theme one last time and climbs to a very high, held note; below it, the Sultan’s theme is now gentle
stops.happening: The Sultan relents. The suite ends in a quiet E major

notice: Compare the Sultan’s theme at the very start of the suite with its last appearance, under the final violin solo. The notes are the same; the mood has completely changed.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The violin solos, Scheherazade’s voice, are played by Steven Staryk, credited on the album.

threads.title: Two voices
threads.body: The Sultan’s heavy [[unison|unison]] and Scheherazade’s violin open the suite and close it. Everything in between is her story.

threads.title: The sea
threads.body: It carries the first movement and wrecks the ship in the last.

threads.title: Colour
threads.body: Rimsky-Korsakov was a master of orchestration and taught it for decades. Almost every instrument gets a solo moment.
